text:
sophia: Hey folks — first day, hi! I connected the company VPN (WireGuard) on my Win11 laptop but from WSL2 I can't reach internal git/repo (git.redwood.internal) or the private docker registry. Browser on Windows can hit them fine. Anyone run into WSL + split-tunnel VPN weirdness?

it-support: Welcome! 
it-support: This is a pretty common WSL2 networking gotcha — WSL has its own virtual NIC and doesn't always pick up Windows VPN routes when split-tunnel is used.

sophia: ahhh ok. Any quick fixes I can try? I'm on corporate laptop with YubiKey SSO and the WireGuard client.

maria: If you can, first try shutting down WSL and then adding a persistent route on Windows for the VPC CIDR so the traffic goes via the VPN adapter.
maria: Steps (PowerShell Admin):

maria: ```powershell
wsl --shutdown
# find VPN adapter interface index
Get-NetAdapter | where {$_.InterfaceDescription -match "WireGuard|EnterpriseVPN"}
# add route (example for 10.240.0.0/16)
netsh interface ipv4 add route 10.240.0.0/16 "Ethernet" <VPNGatewayIp> store=active
# OR with interface index:
route -p ADD 10.240.0.0 MASK 255.255.0.0 <VPNGatewayIp> IF <ifIndex>
```

maria: Replace <VPNGatewayIp> and <ifIndex> with values from your system. That forces Windows to send the VPC range over the VPN and WSL will pick it up after restart.

ben: Another option if you only need git/docker is to use the bastion as a SOCKS proxy from WSL: `ssh -D 1080 me@bastion.redwood` then set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` in your WSL env or configure Docker to use the proxy.

ben: Example SSH on WSL:

ben: ```bash
ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 -D 1080 alice@bastion.redwood:22 -N
export HTTP_PROXY=http://localhost:1080
export HTTPS_PROXY=http://localhost:1080
# then try docker login or git clone
```

it-support: If you're using Docker Desktop, there's also a checkbox in Settings > Resources > Network to use the WSL integration; sometimes toggling fixes DNS. If registry still fails, add the registry hostname to Docker's insecure-registries or configure TLS certs per our internal docs.

sophia: ok trying the route add approach now. How do I find the VPN gateway IP quickly?

maria: In PowerShell: `Get-NetRoute -InterfaceAlias "*VPN*" -AddressFamily IPv4 | Where-Object {$_.DestinationPrefix -ne "0.0.0.0/0"}` or `ipconfig /all` and look for the WireGuard adapter details.

devops-bot: FYI: internal docs -> https://confluence.redwood/infra/wsl-vpn-notes (useful checklist) :white_check_mark:

sophia: route added and wsl --shutdown + restarted. I can now `git clone` the internal repo from WSL and `docker pull` the private image. :tada:

sophia: follow-up — Docker still complained about certs; I added the CA cert to Windows trust store and enabled WSL integration. all good now.

maria: Great! If you want, post the exact `Get-NetAdapter` output (redact MAC) and we can turn this into a tiny onboarding note for other Windows new-hires.

sophia: Will do. Thanks everyone!

ben: Quick tip for the future: add an SSH bastion config in `~/.ssh/config` so you can `ssh internal-host` without passing -J each time.

sophia: Nice. Appreciate the help.
